# Northvale pulled the plug. Your money is safe — and yes, you should be angry.

**Inês — Product Design, Pinha**
Tuesday, 10 November 2026

Everything we know as of today, what we're doing about it, and what you can do right now. No date I can't keep, and no "we apologise for the inconvenience".

---

## If you only read one thing today

1. **Your money is not lost.** It's in a safeguarded account that Northvale cannot touch. We are working to move it to a new partner. Details below.
2. **If you need money out for something urgent** — rent, medical, job loss — write to **urgent@pinha.example** with the subject **URGENTE**. That inbox is separate from the support queue and we work through it on its own.
3. **We'll post an update on the blog every Monday and Thursday** until this is over. If nothing changes, the update will say that nothing changed. If something changes, the update will say that.

That's the short version. The rest is the truth, and it's not comfortable.

---

## What happened

Northvale Payments is the Lithuanian e-money institution that has been holding Pinha's customer money since we launched. Four days ago, on Wednesday 4 November, they emailed us a notice of "commercial termination" with 30 days' notice, citing a "risk appetite review".

On Friday 6 November, at 09:00, they blocked every outgoing transfer. No warning before it. No call. No email saying "we decided to do this early". Deposits stopped as well, and round-ups stopped.

They broke their own notice. Their email gave us until the beginning of December. They didn't wait for their own deadline.

I keep coming back to that word, "risk". Read it again and decide what it means. If a risk review means "we don't want to be looked at closely and we'd rather slam the door than let anyone open it", then that is not risk management. That's cowardice. And on Friday morning, at 09:00, a lot of people in Portugal found out what it looks like when a partner runs.

Their account manager stopped answering our calls on Friday. His phone goes to a voicemail in Lithuanian. As of today, we have had no substantive response from Northvale since the block.

---

## Your money is safe. It's also stuck. Both of those are true.

I need to be precise here, because "safe" and "accessible" are not the same thing and I'm not going to use the first word to hide the second.

Pinha is not a bank. Your balance doesn't sit in a Pinha account we can spend, borrow against, or invest. Your money sits with Northvale, in a safeguarded account, legally separated from Northvale's own money. Northvale cannot use it. They cannot lend it out. They cannot take it to pay staff or rent or a fine. It's yours, and in law it stays yours.

So the money is not lost. It is not gone. It hasn't been taken. Nobody at Northvale can touch it.

But we cannot move it either. Moving it requires Northvale to release the balances file and complete the handover, and Northvale has stopped speaking to us. That's the part that makes me want to put my fist through a desk: our users' money is sitting in a safe place, and the people who are legally obliged to hand it over have gone quiet.

Safe, and out of reach. Today, that's the sentence we have to give you.

---

## The email I read on the metro

One of you wrote to us last week and I read it on my way home, on the metro, standing up.

A woman from Porto. All in capitals. She has been saving for three years for a deposit on a car. The dealership is holding it until Friday 13 November. She found out her money was frozen because our app is where she saved it.

I nearly cried on the Linha Verde, and not because of the car. Because for three years she put her money into an app that says *"your money is always yours. Take it out anytime."* I wrote that sentence. I designed the screen it's on. It's one of the things I'm proudest of in this job, and on Friday morning it stopped being true for reasons that had nothing to do with her and everything to do with how we built the business.

I'm not going to retype her email to make a point. You know what your money is for. That's the entire point of it.

---

## Our mistake, said out loud

While we're talking about who is responsible: us.

Pinha ran on a single payment partner. One. Not because we thought one was enough, but because one was fast, cheap, and it worked, and we were proud of how painless taking money out felt. We did not have a second provider standing by. We did not build the migration playbook before we needed it. On Friday morning, the thing that would have cost us days instead of hours was a fallback we never put in place.

That was a decision, and it was mine as much as anyone's. I drew a screen that promised you something we had not actually built the infrastructure to keep. If that promise had been tested properly, we'd have known we had a single point of failure. Nobody tested it, because everything was working, and that's exactly how you end up here.

So no. This isn't only Northvale's fault, and I'm not going to let the story be about a bad guy in Vilnius so we get to feel cleaner. We trusted one company with your money and we didn't build a plan for the day they changed their mind. We should have had a second partner signed and ready in a drawer. We didn't.

---

## What we're doing

**We've already signed the new partner.** Ostra Bank, in Lisbon. The agreement is done.

**What's left on the migration:**
- Northvale sends us the balances file and releases the money.
- Banco de Portugal approves the handover.

As of today, we have neither. Northvale has not sent the file. The Banco de Portugal approval is in progress and we're pushing it every working day.

**How long once those two things land:** our estimate is **10 to 15 working days**.

I'm not turning that into a date. I know exactly what you're thinking — "so when?" — and I'm not going to hand you a Tuesday in late November as if I could hold it. If I promise you the 24th and it's the 26th, you will have learned a second thing about us today: that we can't be trusted with your money either. Give me the file and the approval, and then I'll give you a date, and it'll be one I can keep.

**We've filed complaints.** On 7 November we filed with the **Banco de Portugal** and with the **Bank of Lithuania**, Northvale's home regulator. Those complaints are the formal channel for putting pressure on a licensed institution that has stopped communicating with the people holding its customers' money.

**Your monthly fee is cancelled for November and December.** For everyone, automatically, no action needed. This is small compared to the rest of it, but there's no reason to keep charging people for a service they can't use. It does not, on its own, unblock anything — I'm not going to dress it up as more than it is.

**Deposits and round-ups are paused.** Since 6 November the app hasn't taken a single euro out of your account, and no new round-ups have been added. Your balance from 6 November is the balance we're fighting to get back to you.

---

## If you're waiting on a reply from us

Since Friday we have received **1,900 support emails**. There are three of us answering them. Our current reply time is about **two days**.

I know that's a bad place to be, especially if you're looking at a bill. Every email gets an answer, and we are working through the queue in order, but I won't pretend three people is enough for 1,900 emails. It isn't.

Two things that will help:

- **If your case is urgent** — rent, a medical bill, you've lost your job — write to **urgent@pinha.example** with the subject **URGENTE**. That's a separate inbox and a separate queue, and we go through it first. We're trying to get individual releases for the worst cases. I can't promise they'll come through, because the decision sits with a company that isn't answering us. But we're asking, and asking is what we can do.
- **If you've already written and your situation has changed**, reply to the same thread rather than starting a new one, so we don't lose track of you.

If your money is in a brokerage, a shared account with someone, or in your partner's name — that doesn't change the fact that it's yours, and it doesn't change who has to hand it over. Write to us anyway.

---

## If you want to add pressure

Our complaints are in. Yours would sit alongside them.

If you live in Portugal, you can file a complaint with the **Banco de Portugal**. If you live in Spain, the **Banco de España** is the right one. And because Northvale is licensed in Lithuania, the **Bank of Lithuania** can hear it too. It takes a paragraph. It costs you an afternoon.

I'm not going to tell you it will speed anything up. What I will say is that there are 14,200 of us in this, and a regulator who has 14,200 individual complaints about one institution is a very different conversation from a regulator who has one.

---

## The last thing

You are allowed to be angry.

Not just at Northvale — at us too, if you want. That's fair. We let one partner hold all the money, we didn't build a backup, and we shipped a promise to 14,200 people that we hadn't made true in the infrastructure. I'd rather have your honest anger than your polite patience, because polite patience is exactly the thing that let us run on a single provider for as long as we did.

Don't calm down on our account. Don't be nice about it. Keep writing, keep complaining, keep telling the truth about what this has been like for you. We'll be here every Monday and Thursday with an update, including the ones where the update is "still nothing".

Your money is safe. We're going to get it to you. And when it's in your account again, we'll fix the thing that should never have been a single point of failure in the first place.

— **Inês**
Product Design, Pinha
